- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often overcorrects upward; cap forecast at recent high or adjust downward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overextension.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is low and price is trending down, model may lag in recognizing the decline; forecast should be adjusted to match recent low trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; consider smoothing or using weighted average of recent 7–14 days for mid-term forecasts.
- If sentiment is high and price is falling, model may misinterpret sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false optimism.
